card.title: Nintendo Switch Not Charging

claims.statement: The Switch's two main charging failure points are M92T36 (custom Rohm USB-C PMIC) and PI3USB (video IC that also matters for charging); both often die with port or cable damage and may not show obvious shorts.
When replacing a port, check caps around both ICs; if a short remains after removing the chip, suspect the CPU. Also check the fuse above the port.
After repair a USB-C meter should show 15 V; around 0.5 A draw is expected—if not, try a new battery and check autoRCM, which can drain the battery below where the brick can charge it.

procedure: Check caps around M92T36 and PI3USB; remove chips to isolate shorts.
Check the fuse above the port.
Confirm 15 V negotiation and ~0.5 A draw.
If no image, recheck PI3USB and check for RCM with Hekate.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
